name: Bronze Age & the Hundred Schools
summary: Shang oracle bones and bronzes; the Zhou dynasty and its classics; in the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods Confucius, Laozi, Mozi, Mencius, Zhuangzi and Han Feizi found Chinese philosophy. Jōmon and Yayoi cultures in Japan; Gojoseon in Korea.

name: The First Empires
summary: Qin unification and the Terracotta Army; the Han dynasty makes Confucianism state orthodoxy, writes the first standard history and invents paper; Buddhism arrives from India; the Six Dynasties produce calligraphy and landscape poetry. Kofun-era Japan and the Three Kingdoms of Korea.

name: The Cosmopolitan Age
summary: Sui and Tang China, the age of Li Bai and Du Fu, Buddhist cave temples and the Silk Road; Japan adopts Chinese writing, law and Buddhism in the Asuka, Nara and early Heian periods; Unified Silla in Korea.

name: Song, Heian & Goryeo
summary: Song China: printing, Neo-Confucianism, monumental landscape painting and the civil-service state, followed by Mongol Yuan rule; Heian court literature (The Tale of Genji) and the warrior Kamakura era in Japan; Goryeo celadon and the Tripitaka Koreana in Korea.

name: Ming, Muromachi & Early Joseon
summary: Ming China's Forbidden City, porcelain, novels and Wang Yangming; Zen culture, Noh theatre and the tea ceremony in Muromachi and Momoyama Japan; Joseon Korea invents the Hangul alphabet.

name: Qing, Edo & Late Joseon
summary: The Manchu Qing dynasty at its height and Dream of the Red Chamber; Tokugawa Japan's peace, kabuki, haiku and ukiyo-e; true-view landscape painting and Silhak practical learning in Korea. Ends with Western gunboats and the opening of Japan.

name: Revolution & Modernisation
summary: Meiji Japan modernises and builds an empire; the Qing falls in 1911 and the May Fourth movement remakes Chinese culture; Korea is annexed by Japan in 1910. New literatures, art schools and ideas meet the West, ending in war.

name: Since 1945
summary: Occupation and economic miracle in Japan; the People's Republic and the Cultural Revolution, then reform; the division of Korea; East Asian film, architecture, literature and art become world forces.
